laws.summary: AI is an independent first-class ability group and must remain the only public AI owner.
AI child capabilities represent provider/runtime channels; business task routing is AI-owned and must not replace child ids.
AI may reason and return structured results only; it may not execute actions or side effects.
local-ai-runtime is an internal execution boundary under AI ownership and must not become a second public AI system.
paid and future API AI children are visible but disabled by policy and must fail closed.
AI outputs must be cleaned before persistence and must not leak AI runtime contracts into Forensics public ownership.
AI keeps a single public contract and does not leak child, adapter, prompt, or legacy internals.
ai-capability inspector is the only enforcement owner for AI topology, runtime pipeline, prompt truth, and anti-escape checks.
AI owns the Prompt Contract Registry; prompt execution must resolve by promptContractId/version/catalog, never by hardcoded prompt text.
Prompt contracts must declare full governed metadata and must be hashable, strict, and audit-proof.
Prompt contracts may guide reasoning only and must not command actions, bypass security, or make final mission decisions.
AI runtime must resolve prompt execution by promptContractId and execute a governed runtime pipeline with typed failures.
AI timeout, cancellation, idempotency, concurrency, and circuit breaker state must be governed and proof-backed.
AI result proof must be complete, chain-linked, raw-output-backed, and impossible to fake as success.
AI output boundary must recursively block action authority, browser authority, Forensics authority, and command authority.
inspector plus generated artifacts plus audit runner is the only enforcement chain.
Map Prompt Contract Governance must be enforced by AST, schema, and negative proof.
Prompt contract and map binding drift is audit-blocking.
GrassEye uses one fixed ability-group constitution and one execution chain.
every ability group owns one public contract and one child-boundary catalog.
Commander, Nerve Bus, and Orchestration each have one fixed authority boundary.
runtime proof minimum fields are fixed across every governed execution.
every governed execution must leave evidence, log, and trace.
ability groups must keep hard boundaries and topology must reflect ownership.
Capability Catalog is a generated read model, not a new owner.
AI-generated map authoring must use the governed capability catalog.
active source files must stay atomic and must not exceed Code Purity Phase 3.5 file-size limits.
touched oversized files must be split before new logic is added.
functions must stay small, shallow, and single-purpose.
classes and objects must not become god objects.
owner boundaries must be counted at real capability-owner granularity.
imports and exports must not create hidden broad ownership or barrel laundering.
files must have one role and must not mix schema, runtime, validation, execution, persistence, and decision responsibilities.
dead code, fake runtime paths, mocks, placeholders, and temporary bypasses must not survive in active source truth.
refactors must reduce ownership, file size, complexity, and active paths rather than adding compatibility bridges.
disaster files must be identified, blocked, and physically split before meaningful feature debugging continues.
all active code-purity laws must be proven by real enforcement, generated audit artifacts, runner execution, and negative proof.
type-safety and escape hatches must not be used to bypass purity enforcement.
code-purity enforcement must produce inventories, remediation queues, and physical split plans.
code-purity remediation must use physical deletion and physical splitting, not cosmetic renaming.
Commander Console is the only owner of human command entry and review-disposition entry.
Commander command envelope must be explicit, map/platform-safe, idempotent, timeout-governed, and semantically validated.
Commander read models are read-only Commander-owned view records sourced from governed read-model ports.
Commander must not become Orchestration, Nerve Bus, AI, Forensics, browser/action owner, or storage owner.
Commander package must have one canonical root, real child folders, one child registry, one runtime pipeline, and no compat bridge.
Commander runtime result and proof must preserve command/read chain and must never use fake success, null proof, warning-only pass, or throw from public boundary.
Commander task-template and map-import UX may display governed map lifecycle but must not become map execution, validation, activation, or runtime truth.
Commander enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, generated artifacts, runner, and negative proof.
debug-loop is local development tooling and must not be registered as an active ability group, runtime owner, or production capability owner.
debug-loop may start missions only through Commander public contract and must not directly dispatch Nerve Bus, Orchestration, or ability actions.
debug-loop must not execute direct browser/page/platform operations during mission runtime.
debug-loop must not write production Forensics proof, evidence packets, activation snapshots, or active registry truth.
debug-loop map-authoring harness may create input/prompt artifacts but must not bypass map-plugin lifecycle or execute generated maps.
debug-loop scenario files describe user/operator intent and success/failure signals; they must not contain executable ability logic or direct platform automation logic.
debug-loop repair packets are diagnostic artifacts and must not become code, proof, policy, or runtime truth.
debug-loop boundary must be machine-enforced by owner-local inspector, negative proof, and package scripts.
Forensics Persistence is the only final evidence-ledger owner and must not be bypassed by local-data, runtime, workbench, Commander, AI, or action abilities.
child abilities must be persistence behaviors and every child must write exactly one governed Forensics record type.
Forensics writes and links records only; it must not reason, verify, decide, act, or reconstruct business truth.
Forensics public contract must be Forensics-native and must not leak legacy business or runtime type sovereignty.
every Forensics record and result must preserve the full execution chain and must be replayable.
storage must be a generic record-store port and old store ownership must stay outside the canonical Forensics root.
Forensics writes must be policy-gated, integrity-gated, idempotent, and append-safe.
Forensics enforcement must be AST/symbol/import-graph based and connected to runner and negative proof.
Forensics is the only owner allowed to promote transient screenshot artifacts into retained evidence or legal hold, and it owns cleanup-ledger truth.
Geometry Guard is the only owner of governed executable geometry safety gating.
Geometry Guard public contract must stay clean, native, and independent.
Geometry Guard input must carry full chain fields, source refs, coordinate evidence, idempotency, and policy.
Geometry Guard must validate finite geometry, coordinate space, scale mapping, bounds, click safety, and execution target without silent clamp.
Geometry Guard must use one fixed gate pipeline and must remain side-effect free.
Geometry Guard result and runtime proof must preserve real upstream chain, gate decisions, refs, and normalized geometry.
downstream execution owners must consume only Geometry Guard approved executable geometry and must not redo mapping.
Geometry Guard enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
local-ai-runtime must expose one governed startup readiness contract and must not be started ad hoc by consumers.
map packages are declarative route data consumed by Orchestration, not runtime code, child abilities, or new owners.
map packages must pass import, quarantine, validation, human approval, activation, active registry, and rollback lifecycle before runtime consumption.
map package schema must contain complete governance metadata and must not depend on runtime truth as package authority.
map packages must never carry executable payloads, runtime code, prompt text, shell scripts, dynamic imports, handlers, or direct ability control.
map packages may reference prompt contracts but must not own prompt content or create prompt double-truth.
AI-generated map packages must be authored against governed catalogs and remain draft/quarantine until all gates and human approval pass.
capability catalog is a generated read model used for authoring and validation; it must not become runtime truth or a second ability registry.
branch condition DSL must be schema-declared, closed, non-executable, and able to reference declared outputSchemaRef fields.
ordinary and developer map surfaces must stay separate, and Commander must not activate or mutate maps without governed validation/approval path.
map activation, validation, approval, prompt binding, and authoring must produce Forensics-compatible proof records.
user-facing map explanation must translate route data into understandable task flow without exposing runtime internals in ordinary mode.
map-plugin-package enforcement must close through owner-local AST/schema/reference inspector, runner, and negative proof.
advanced AI map generation must receive a complete Map Authoring Input Package; missing catalogs or policies must block generation.
capability catalog must be detailed enough for advanced AI to generate maps without inventing abilities.
prompt contract and output schema catalogs must define every AI step and branchable field used by maps.
safety, human approval, evidence, PAV, Forensics, privacy, secret, rate-limit, and platform policies must be first-class inputs to map authoring.
map-plugin-package enforcement must prove Map Authoring Input Package completeness, generated-map safety, and lifecycle boundaries in addition to existing map package governance.
Mouse Click is the only owner of governed primitive click execution.
Mouse Click boundary stays pure and cannot compute coordinates, remap geometry, verify outcomes, or perform foreign owner work.
Mouse Click input must carry full chain fields, Geometry Guard allow proof, executable coordinate, safety policy, source refs, idempotency, and timeout policy.
Mouse Click must run one fixed gate pipeline and execute exactly one primitive click only after all gates pass.
Mouse Click result must mean primitive click only and must hand off to Post-action Verification.
Mouse Click result and runtime proof must preserve real upstream chain, gate decisions, primitive refs, timeout/cancellation, idempotency, and PAV handoff.
Mouse Click children are narrow primitive bindings and must use unified runtime.
Mouse Click enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Mouse Scroll is the only owner of governed primitive scroll execution.
Mouse Scroll boundary stays pure and cannot compute coordinates, remap geometry, verify outcomes, or perform foreign owner work.
Mouse Scroll input must carry full chain fields, Geometry Guard allow proof, explicit direction/magnitude/repeat, safety policy, source refs, idempotency, and timeout policy.
Scroll direction, magnitude, delta, and repeat are input/policy only, not child capability or hidden loop.
Mouse Scroll must run one fixed gate pipeline and execute primitive scroll only after all gates pass.
Mouse Scroll result must mean primitive scroll only and must hand off to Post-action Verification.
Mouse Scroll result and runtime proof must preserve real upstream chain, gate decisions, primitive refs, repeat proofs, timeout/cancellation, idempotency, and PAV handoff.
Mouse Scroll children are narrow primitive bindings and must use unified runtime.
Mouse Scroll enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Nerve Bus is the only owner of governed command/result transport between Commander Console, Orchestration, AI, and Ability Groups.
All Nerve Bus envelopes must preserve complete mission/map/step/capability/prompt chain fields and must fail closed when chain truth is missing.
Nerve Bus has exactly six governed logical channels and must not create business-specific or platform-specific transport channels.
Nerve Bus validates, routes, times out, records proof, and returns typed envelopes; it must not make mission, map, AI, action, or storage decisions.
Nerve Bus must run a fixed fail-closed transport pipeline.
Nerve Bus result semantics must be typed, correlated, payload-ref first, and proof-backed.
Nerve Bus transfer proof must preserve full chain, timing, gate decisions, handler decision, payload refs, and correlation refs.
Nerve Bus AI transport must carry Prompt Contract references only and must not carry raw prompt truth.
Nerve Bus children are narrow channel bindings and must use unified runtime.
Nerve Bus enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Open Ability Group is the only owner of governed open behavior.
Open boundary stays pure and cannot own state, verification, AI, screenshot, visual target, action, Forensics, or mission branching truth.
Open input must carry governed chain fields, target profile context, source proof, timeout, and idempotency.
Open must run a fixed target/profile/session/navigation/idempotency/timeout/page-state-handoff pipeline.
Open success requires page-state handoff and must not claim page-state readiness or action-result verification.
Open result and runtime proof must preserve real upstream chain, gate decisions, browser attempt refs, timeout/cancellation, idempotency, and page-state handoff.
child capabilities are narrow target-open bindings and must use unified Open runtime.
Open must support governed macOS local program launch as a first-class target and must not confuse local program opening with local workbench URL opening.
Open enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Orchestration is the only owner of mission flow, operational map selection, mission state, step state, branch evaluation, and finalization.
Operational maps are declarative approved packages consumed by Orchestration, not executable code, child abilities, or second runtimes.
Orchestration must freeze map activation snapshot and must not reselect latest map during mission execution.
Orchestration dispatches only through Nerve Bus envelopes and public ability group contracts.
Orchestration step execution must follow the active map and enforce preconditions, PAV after actions, evidence routing, loop guard, and transition closure.
Prompt selection is map-owned and frozen; Orchestration must not build raw prompts or hardcode prompt selection.
Orchestration may request persistence but must not hide finalization, branch, candidate, or delivery-state ownership under Forensics.
Orchestration result and runtime proof must preserve command, map activation, state transition, dispatch envelope, branch, loop, timeout, idempotency, and finalization chain.
Orchestration children are mission lifecycle and transition actions only and must use unified runtime.
Orchestration enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Page State is the only owner of governed current-page state classification.
Page State boundary is pure and may only classify from governed inputs.
Page State input must carry full chain fields, snapshot proof, observations, evidence refs, policies, and open handoff.
Observations and evidence must be source-bound, fresh, and from allowed owners.
Page State output must be evidence-backed and cannot claim action-result verification truth.
Page State runtime proof must preserve real chain, gate decisions, source refs, and state fingerprint.
child capabilities are narrow state classifiers and must use unified runtime gates.
Page State enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Post-action Verification is the only owner of governed action-result truth.
PAV boundary stays pure and cannot execute actions, capture evidence, call AI, or persist final evidence.
PAV input must carry action proof, source action refs, expected outcome, before/after evidence, observations, and chain fields.
PAV must verify with bounded observations and evidence; before/after requirements must be enforced by policy.
PAV must return typed verification decision only: verified, failed, or review_required.
PAV runtime proof must preserve the same chain as input and result, without fabricated mission/run truth.
child capabilities must be narrow verification behaviors and must use unified executor/runtime proof path.
PAV enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Screenshot Ability Group is the only owner of governed screenshot capture, image artifact truth, coordinate-space truth, and scale mapping.
Screenshot boundary stays pure: capture, lossless optimize, crop/region, AI input preparation, artifact refs, and proof only.
Screenshot input must carry full chain fields, source proof, privacy policy, capture policy, idempotency, and timeout.
Screenshot coordinate spaces and scale mapping must be explicit, lossless where claimed, and non-executable until downstream governance.
Screenshot runtime must use one fixed gate pipeline and fail closed on privacy, source, session, timeout, artifact, and output-boundary violations.
Screenshot result and runtime proof must preserve real chain, artifact refs, hashes, source refs, scale mapping, gate decisions, and parity.
Screenshot child capabilities are narrow capture/transform bindings and must use unified Screenshot runtime.
Screenshot enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
Screenshot artifacts are transient runtime materials by default and must carry lifecycle manifest, retention, TTL, quota, and non-self-promotion truth.
GrassEye must operate only with user-authorized local accounts while minimizing sensitive capture and never bypassing platform security.
Prompt contracts and AI-generated maps must never request sensitive secrets or hidden bypass channels.
Sensitive tasks require review gates before mutating user data or high-risk platform state.
startup must complete update preflight and local AI readiness gate before mission runtime becomes available.
Text Input is the only owner of governed text/key writing primitives.
Text Input is write-only and must not generate text, locate targets, decide target safety, or verify final page state.
Text Input input must carry full mission/map/step/capability chain, approved text proof, verified target proof, focus proof, and Nerve Bus envelope refs.
Text Input executes only through governed execution, clipboard, and clock ports with AbortSignal/timeout and fail-closed semantics.
Text Input must treat sensitive text and clipboard content as non-persistent transient material and must record only refs, hashes, redacted previews, and policy decisions.
Text Input success is primitive write/key success only and must hand off to Post-action Verification.
Text Input runtime proof must preserve full chain, target proof, focus proof, text proof, clipboard proof, primitive proof, PAV handoff, and redaction decisions.
Text Input children are narrow execution bindings and must use unified runtime.
Text Input enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
all external uncertainty must become validated domain types before it can drive actions or records.
Visual Target is the only owner of governed visual target result normalization.
Visual Target boundary stays pure: it validates, normalizes, selects, and builds handoff only.
Visual Target input must carry full chain fields, source proof, candidate proof, policy, and idempotency.
coordinate-space truth must be explicit; Visual Target output is not executable until Geometry Guard.
Visual Target runtime must use a single gate pipeline and fail closed on ambiguity, stale evidence, source mismatch, and critical data quality.
Visual Target result and runtime proof must preserve real chain, source refs, candidate refs, gate decisions, coordinate transform trace, and Geometry Guard handoff.
child capabilities are narrow target bindings and must use unified Visual Target runtime.
Visual Target enforcement must close through owner-local AST/symbol/import-graph inspector, runner, and negative proof.
